description.en: Zimbabwe observes a range of public holidays reflecting its national history, culture, and traditions. These holidays affect work schedules, school terms, and travel plans across the country.

sections.title: About Zimbabwe
sections.content: Zimbabwe, officially the Republic of Zimbabwe, is a landlocked country in Southeast Africa, between the Zambezi and Limpopo River, bordered by South Africa to the south, Botswana to the southwest, Zambia to the north, and Mozambique to the east. The capital and largest city is Harare, and the second largest is Bulawayo.

sections.title: Important Notice
sections.content: Public holiday dates and observance rules can change, especially when holidays fall on weekends. Always confirm critical dates with official Zimbabwe government sources when planning travel, payroll, or business operations.

sections.title: How Zimbabwe's Public Holidays Are Observed
sections.content:
On most public and bank holidays:

Banks and government offices are closed.
Schools are closed.
Some businesses operate reduced hours.
Public transport and retail services may run modified schedules.
Private businesses are not legally required to close but often adjust operating hours.

sections.title: Why Zimbabwe's Public Holidays Matter
sections.content:
Understanding Zimbabwe's public holidays helps with:

Business and payroll planning.
School and academic scheduling.
Travel and accommodation planning.
Avoiding service disruptions.
Both residents and visitors benefit from knowing when closures and peak travel periods are likely.

q.en: Are all public holidays observed nationwide in Zimbabwe?

a.en: While many holidays are national, some observances may be limited to specific regions, states, or territories.

q.en: Do businesses and stores close on public holidays in Zimbabwe?

a.en: Generally yes. Government offices, banks, and schools are closed. Essential services and some retail sectors may remain open or operate on reduced hours.

q.en: What happens if a public holiday falls on a weekend in Zimbabwe?

a.en: In many cases, if a national holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the observance is moved to the following Monday, though this depends on specific local laws and the holiday in question.

q.en: Are public transport services affected by holidays in Zimbabwe?

a.en: Yes, public transportation often runs on a reduced Sunday or holiday schedule during national public holidays.

q.en: Are employees entitled to paid time off on public holidays in Zimbabwe?

a.en: Most full-time employees are legally entitled to a paid day off on national public holidays. Those who are required to work are typically eligible for premium pay or a substitute day off.
